title: Why Good Enough Wins | Principles of Management Ep 24
description:
What do you do when there are too many options to check? Chai Corner is ready to open its sixth outlet, but the city has 4,000 streets, and checking every one would take a year. In this animated lesson, Ravi learns why perfect takes too long, and how to choose good enough on purpose.

You will meet Herbert A. Simon, who studied how people in organisations really decide, wrote Administrative Behavior in 1947, and won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1978 for his research on decision making in organisations. We explain bounded rationality (people try to be rational, but their thinking has limits), the three bounds of information, time and brain power, and Simon's own word, satisfice, which joins satisfy and suffice. Then we watch Ravi satisfice live: three must haves, one small area, street by street, until street three passes every check. We compare optimising with satisficing, see must haves, small search areas, rules of thumb, deadlines and stopping at good enough at work today, and look at the human side honestly: satisficing is fast and fits real people, but set your must haves too low and you settle for something poor.

This is Episode 24 of our Principles of Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
